title: Bix dictating saxophone choruses and trumpet voicings
summary: Bix dictated saxophone choruses such as Ostrich Walk and Challis harmonized three-part trumpet passages under his lead.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You know, it was in a certain range. Piano you can go all over the piano. You can play up here, it was down around here, you could go from down here up there, and from up there down here. But the cornet you have to stay in a certain range. Now, he does that on the piano. Now, he does that also with few exceptions, few flourishes. He sat down and dictated to me some choruses and that would be for Trumbauer. The chorus of 'Ostrich Walk,' for instance, (sings) , that was for

saxophone. He had a very good idea, although I know he didn't play sax, he didn't know anything about it. I put it in the key, but he did have the idea of the way he wanted the saxophone to sound, and he used some saxophonistic curlicues or phrases that could be done nicely on a saxophone.

Now, on his trumpet, you know, there was more of a blare, we did a lot of three-part trumpet things together and all I did was harmonize though, like that thing on "Sunday." (sings). Now, that's typically trumpet there. I'd come under his fingers, but the other two guys when they got the other two parts, they followed right along.

That's all rhythmic and that's all cornet style of playing. So he had an excellent idea of that type of instrumentation, and in some of his things, he puts in a few things that could only come out right if you gave them to a horn and woodwinds, a lot.
